context.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency while ensuring regulatory compliance, auditability, and resilience for low-bandwidth connections.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU/US) and Licensed Clinicians
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform (GCP-hosted)
- National E-Prescription Gateways (EU) and US Pharmacy Networks
- AI Symptom Checker Engine
- Compliance / Regulatory Authorities and Medical Licensing Board Services

## Relationships
- Patient/Clinician to Platform via HTTPS/WebRTC (optimized for <300 kbit/s connections)
- Platform to External Pharmacies/Gateways via mTLS with REST/FHIR payloads
- Platform to Medical Licensing Board Services via REST/HTTPS with local caching
- Platform to Compliance Authorities via OAuth2/mTLS for secure audit export

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP) deployed in `europe-west3` (EU) and `us-central1` (US) for regional data residency
- WebRTC Selective Forwarding Units (SFUs) deployed locally in each region for adaptive video streaming
- Cloud KMS with regional customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) and TLS 1.3 for data protection
- Cloud Audit Logs with Object Lock for append-only, tamper-proof AI traceability
- OAuth2 and Web Application Firewall (WAF) for secure API gateway enforcement

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict HIPAA and GDPR compliance by physically separating EU and US health data into dedicated GCP regions while enabling cross-border access through explicit, token-based consent. Additionally, it ensures medical device traceability and high availability for rural patients via local SFUs and immutable audit logging.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency and compliance using isolated cloud deployments.

## Key Elements
- Patients & Licensed Clinicians
- Compliance Officers / Auditors
- Regional Ingress (Cloud Load Balancing & Envoy)
- Web/Mobile Frontend (Flutter)
- Telehealth Service (Go / WebRTC)
- Prescription & Record Service (Java / Spring Boot)
- AI Orchestrator & Audit Service (Python / FastAPI)
- Consent & Identity Service (Keycloak / PostgreSQL)

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians to Regional Ingress via HTTPS / WSS
- Frontend to Telehealth Service via WebRTC / UDP (adaptive bitrate streaming)
- Internal Containers to Internal Containers via gRPC with mTLS
- Prescription Service to National E-Prescription Gateways (EU) and US Pharmacy Networks via HL7 FHIR / national standards
- AI Orchestrator to Regional Cloud Storage via WORM file protocols

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Deployed in `europe-west3` and `us-central1` for strict regional data residency
- Flutter: Enables offline-first client state for low-bandwidth rural connections (<300 kbit/s)
- Go / WebRTC: Manages low-latency media streams with global regional TURN relays
- Java / Spring Boot: Abstracts fragmented EU and US e-prescription standards
- Python / FastAPI: Orchestrates AI symptom checker with immutable audit logging
- Keycloak / PostgreSQL: Manages identity, OAuth2/OIDC, and per-purpose GDPR/HIPAA consent

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict regional data isolation between the EU and US to comply with GDPR and HIPAA mandates. Regional container redundancy ensures high availability, auditability, and low-bandwidth resilience for rural users.

Regional Ingress.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency while ensuring high availability for rural, low-bandwidth users.

## Key Elements
* Patients and Licensed Clinicians (End Users)
* Compliance Officers and Auditors (Personas)
* Regional Ingress Container (GCP Cloud Armor, Global External HTTP(S) Load Balancer, Envoy Edge Proxy, Envoy WASM Route & Policy Enforcer)
* Downstream Containers (Flutter Frontend, Go/WebRTC Telehealth Service, Java/Spring Boot Prescription Service, Python/FastAPI AI Orchestrator, Keycloak Identity Service)
* External Systems (EU National E-Prescription Gateways, US Pharmacy Networks, AI Symptom Checker Engine)

## Relationships
* Patients & Clinicians -> Regional Ingress: Accesses platform features via HTTPS and WSS
* Compliance Officers -> Regional Ingress: Accesses audit logs and controls via HTTPS
* Global External HTTP(S) Load Balancer -> Envoy Edge Proxy: Forwards TCP/HTTPS streams via internal VPC
* Envoy Edge Proxy -> Route & Policy Enforcer (WASM): Invokes in-process synchronous inspection
* Route & Policy Enforcer -> Downstream Containers: Routes verified traffic via gRPC and mTLS (SPIFFE/SPIRE)

## Technology Stack
* GCP (europe-west3, us-central1): Cloud provider and target regions enforcing data residency
* Cloud Armor: Edge-level DDoS defense, adaptive rate limiting, and geo-detection
* Envoy Edge Proxy: TLS 1.3 termination, WebSocket upgrades, and traffic routing
* Envoy WASM Extension: Custom policy enforcement, JWT validation, and geo-pinning
* ArgoCD: GitOps-based regional configuration deployments
* Prometheus & OpenTelemetry: Observability and distributed tracing for latency tracking

## Rationale
This architecture uses edge-level geo-steering and regional ingress isolation to strictly enforce GDPR and HIPAA data residency constraints (R-05). Deploying Envoy with WASM and mTLS secures cross-border boundaries while supporting low-bandwidth optimization (R-06) and verifiable audit trails (R-07).

Web/Mobile Frontend.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, offline resilience for rural users, and regulatory compliance (GDPR/HIPAA/MDR).

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Patients and Licensed Clinicians.
- **External Systems**: EU National E-Prescription Gateways, US Pharmacy Networks, AI Symptom Checker Engine, Compliance Authorities.
- **Containers**: Web/Mobile Frontend (Flutter), Regional Ingress (Cloud Load Balancing & Envoy), Telehealth Service (Go/WebRTC), Prescription & Record Service (Java/Spring Boot), AI Orchestrator & Audit Service (Python/FastAPI), Consent & Identity Service (Keycloak/PostgreSQL).
- **Frontend Components**: Routing & State Component (Hive/SQLite), Video Consultation Component, Consent & Triage UI Component, Region-Aware API Client.

## Relationships
- Web/Mobile Frontend -> Regional Ingress: Routes all API, WebSocket, and WebRTC traffic [HTTPS, WebSockets, WebRTC / TLS 1.3].
- Web/Mobile Frontend -> Telehealth Service: Streams video and audio consultations [WebRTC / UDP].
- Web/Mobile Frontend -> AI Orchestrator & Audit Service: Requests symptom check triage and recommendations [HTTPS/REST].
- Web/Mobile Frontend -> Consent & Identity Service: Authenticates users and manages granular consents [OAuth2/OIDC].

## Technology Stack
- **Flutter**: Cross-platform web/mobile frontend framework chosen for offline-first capabilities.
- **SQLite/Hive with AES-256**: Local storage encrypted via device hardware keystores (Android Keystore/iOS Keychain) for offline rural support (R-06).
- **Go & WebRTC**: Telehealth streaming engine supporting adaptive bitrate scaling below 300 kbit/s.
- **Python / FastAPI**: AI orchestrator for traceable symptom checker logging (R-07).
- **GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`)**: Cloud provider and regions enforcing strict data residency (R-05).

## Rationale
This architecture uses an offline-first Flutter client with hardware-backed encryption to maintain rural availability and security without violating compliance. Dynamic regional API pinning and isolated GCP deployments guarantee that EU and US health data remain strictly segregated per regulatory mandates.

Telehealth Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance (GDPR/HIPAA), and resilient media streaming for rural areas.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Licensed Clinicians (Users)
- Web/Mobile Frontend (Flutter)
- Regional Ingress (GCP Cloud Load Balancing & Envoy)
- Telehealth Service (Go / WebRTC)
- Consent & Identity Service (Keycloak / PostgreSQL)
- Prescription & Record Service (Java / Spring Boot)
- AI Orchestrator & Audit Service (Python / FastAPI)
- National E-Prescription Gateways (EU) and US Pharmacy Networks
- Internal Telehealth Components: Signaling Component, Media Gateway (SFU / Pion), Bandwidth Adaptation Engine, Session Audit Logger, Session Lifecycle Manager

## Relationships
- Web/Mobile Frontend -> Telehealth Service: Streams video consultations [WebRTC / UDP]
- Signaling Component -> Consent & Identity Service: Validates short-lived session tokens [gRPC / mTLS]
- Session Lifecycle Manager -> Prescription & Record Service: Logs completed session metadata and feedback triggers [gRPC]
- Telehealth Service -> Regional TURN Relays: Relays media streams under strict data residency constraints [TLS/DTLS/SRTP]

## Technology Stack
- Go: Chosen for high-throughput, low-latency media handling in the Telehealth Service
- WebRTC / Pion & SRTP: Provides real-time communication and secure end-to-end media encryption
- GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Enforces regional data residency for EU and US health data
- gRPC with mTLS: Ensures secure, efficient inter-container communication

## Rationale
This architecture uses regional GCP deployments and isolated media gateways to satisfy strict GDPR, HIPAA, and data residency mandates. Furthermore, the Go-based WebRTC stack with dynamic bandwidth adaptation guarantees consultation availability even on unstable rural connections below 300 kbit/s.

Prescription & Record Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Prescription & Record Service is a secure, regionally isolated enterprise container within the Cross-Border Telehealth Platform responsible for processing, translating, and securely dispatching e-prescriptions. It bridges fragmented national e-prescription standards across the EU and US while strictly enforcing data residency and patient consent mandates.

## Key Elements
* Prescription API Controller (Spring MVC)
* FHIR / National Adapter Engine (Spring Integration / Camel)
* Audit & Compliance Logger (Spring AOP)
* Prescription State & Idempotency Manager (Spring Data JPA / Redis)
* External Gateways: National E-Prescription Gateways (EU) and US Pharmacy Networks
* Supporting Services: Consent & Identity Service (Keycloak / PostgreSQL), Regional Pub/Sub (GCP)

## Relationships
* Prescription API Controller -> Consent & Identity Service: Validates patient consent and OAuth 2.0 JWT tokens via gRPC with mTLS
* Prescription API Controller -> Prescription State & Idempotency Manager: Checks and stores idempotency tokens via JDBC and Redis
* FHIR / National Adapter Engine -> Regional Pub/Sub: Publishes asynchronous prescription payloads for decoupled dispatch
* FHIR / National Adapter Engine -> External Gateways: Sends HL7 FHIR and national standard payloads via outbound HTTPS/TLS 1.3 with mutual authentication

## Technology Stack
* Java / Spring Boot: Chosen for robust enterprise integration, security tooling, and ecosystem maturity.
* Spring Integration / Camel: Implements the Strategy pattern for dynamic payload routing across fragmented e-prescription standards.
* GCP Memorystore & Cloud Pub/Sub: Provides high-availability Redis caching for idempotency and asynchronous decoupling for unstable networks.
* GCP Secret Manager & CMEK: Secures mTLS keys, API credentials, and ensures data-at-rest encryption aligned with regional boundaries.

## Rationale
This architecture isolates regional health data in GCP (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`) to satisfy GDPR and HIPAA residency mandates. Asynchronous queuing, idempotency caching, and resilience patterns ensure reliable e-prescription delivery despite unstable rural connectivity and external gateway latency.

AI Orchestrator & Audit Service.analysis:
## Overview
A cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients on GCP. It ensures strict regional data residency, regulatory compliance, and traceability under GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR.

## Key Elements
* Patients & Licensed Clinicians
* Compliance Officers & Medical Quality Auditors
* Regional Ingress (Cloud Load Balancing & Envoy)
* Web/Mobile Frontend (Flutter)
* Telehealth Service (Go / WebRTC)
* Prescription & Record Service (Java / Spring Boot)
* AI Orchestrator & Audit Service (Python / FastAPI)
* Consent & Identity Service (Keycloak / PostgreSQL)
* External AI Symptom Checker Engine, National E-Prescription Gateways (EU), and US Pharmacy Networks

## Relationships
* Patients / Clinicians -> Regional Ingress: HTTPS / WebRTC
* Web/Mobile Frontend -> Regional Ingress: REST / gRPC with mTLS
* AI Orchestrator -> AI Symptom Checker Engine: gRPC / HTTPS with timeout handling
* AI Orchestrator -> Telehealth Service: gRPC with mTLS and SPIFFE ID verification
* AI Orchestrator -> Regional WORM Storage: Encrypted audit writes via Cloud KMS

## Technology Stack
* Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Deployment in `europe-west3` and `us-central1` for strict regional data residency.
* Python / FastAPI: Core framework for the AI Orchestrator and audit services.
* Keycloak / PostgreSQL: Identity management and regional consent tracking with JWT-based RBAC.
* Redis / NATS: Encrypted local message broker for asynchronous audit ingestion.
* gRPC with mTLS: Secure internal service-to-service communication.
* GCP Cloud KMS & Secret Manager: Regional envelope encryption and dynamic secret injection.

## Rationale
Isolated regional GKE deployments on GCP guarantee that EU and US health data never cross borders without explicit consent. Asynchronous cryptographic logging and strict RBAC satisfy stringent EU MDR traceability and HIPAA/GDPR compliance mandates.

Consent & Identity Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. The architecture enforces regional data residency and strict privacy compliance.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Licensed Clinicians (Users)
- Web/Mobile Frontend (Flutter)
- Consent & Identity Service (Keycloak / PostgreSQL)
- Telehealth Service (Go / WebRTC)
- Prescription & Record Service (Java / Spring Boot)
- AI Orchestrator & Audit Service (Python / FastAPI)
- Regional Ingress (Cloud Load Balancing & Envoy)

## Relationships
- Web/Mobile Frontend -> Consent & Identity Service: Authenticates users and manages consent [OAuth2/OIDC / HTTPS]
- Telehealth Service -> Consent & Identity Service: Validates identity and authorization [gRPC with mTLS]
- Prescription & Record Service -> Consent & Identity Service: Validates prescription access [gRPC with mTLS]
- All internal services -> WORM Storage: Streams immutable audit logs [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- GCP (europe-west3, us-central1): Guarantees strict regional data residency for EU and US compliance.
- Keycloak / PostgreSQL (Cloud SQL): Manages identity, OAuth2/OIDC, and purpose-based GDPR/HIPAA consent.
- Redis (Memorystore): Provides low-latency token caching and revocation checks.
- Istio / Anthos Service Mesh: Enforces strict mTLS and SPIFFE ID verification.

## Rationale
Regional deployment in GCP isolates EU and US health data to satisfy strict GDPR and HIPAA residency mandates. Using Keycloak with custom SPIs and short-lived tokens ensures secure, traceable, and performant consent management.
